paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to take from this one. Jesus says, "The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath." (Luke 6:5) Lord means the Sabbath answers to Him, not the other way around. Those Pharisees were so busy watching the rules that they missed who was standing right in front of them.

Now look at the man with the withered hand. The scribes and Pharisees were watching Jesus closely, looking for a reason to accuse Him (Luke 6:7). Jesus knew their thoughts, and He still told the man, "Get up and stand among us." (Luke 6:8) Then He asked, "which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?" (Luke 6:9) I think that question was meant to make them stop and think about what the day was for.

So here's the lesson for your baker's heart. You can keep every rule on the shelf and still miss Jesus, because the point of the Sabbath was never to keep people from good. And look at the end: the man stretched out his hand and it was restored, while the others were filled with rage (Luke 6:10-11). Same Jesus, same hand, two different reactions. Friend, spend your time with Him, and let Him make you new.
